title: Network Security - Secure Remote Administration Protocol
description: Networks and network devices shall be secured, managed and controlled to protect information in systems and applications; enforce SSHv2.
rationale: Protects administrative control channels against eavesdropping and tampering.

title: Network Security - Prohibition of Cleartext Protocols (Telnet)
description: Insecure legacy cleartext protocols such as Telnet must be eliminated across network infrastructure.
rationale: Cleartext transmission violates confidentiality safeguards for sensitive management data.

title: Network Security - Prohibition of Cleartext HTTP Management
description: Unencrypted HTTP management interfaces must be disabled on all network assets.
rationale: Prevents interception of administrative credentials across internal network segments.

title: Secure Authentication - Password Length and Complexity
description: Secure authentication technologies and procedures shall be implemented based on information access restrictions; enforce >= 14 chars.
rationale: Ensures strength of administrative authenticators.

title: User Endpoint Devices - Automatic Session Inactivity Lock/Timeout
description: Inactive administrative sessions shall automatically terminate within 10 minutes (600 seconds).
rationale: Mitigates unauthorized session use when administrators step away.

title: Logging - Centralized Security Event Logging
description: Logs that record activities, exceptions, faults and other relevant events shall be produced, stored, protected and analyzed.
rationale: Guarantees log availability and immutability for forensic readiness.

title: Clock Synchronization - Network Time Protocol
description: The clocks of information processing systems within the organization shall be synchronized to approved time sources.
rationale: Ensures reliable timeline reconstruction across multi-source incident investigation.

title: Use of Cryptography - Transport Layer Security for Management (HTTPS)
description: Rules for the effective use of cryptography, including cryptographic key management, shall be defined and implemented.
rationale: Protects confidentiality of sensitive management web interfaces.

title: Configuration Management - Standardized Secure Baseline Enforcement (AAA)
description: Configurations, including security configurations, of hardware, software, services and networks shall be established, documented, implemented, monitored and reviewed.
rationale: Centralized AAA enforces organizational identity standards and access controls across assets.

title: Network Security - Disable Insecure FTP File Transfer Daemon
description: Insecure legacy file transfer daemons must be disabled across all networking infrastructure components.
rationale: Mitigates plaintext password exposure and unauthenticated file access.

title: User Endpoint Devices - Disable Unsecured Auxiliary Management Ports
description: Uncontrolled hardware interfaces and auxiliary ports must be disabled to enforce boundary controls.
rationale: Prevents unauthorized physical and dial-in backdoor access.

title: Use of Cryptography - Enable Password Hash Encryption Service
description: Cryptographic controls shall be applied to protect passwords stored within system configuration files.
rationale: Prevents plain-text disclosure of credentials in configuration archives.

title: Secure Authentication - Protection Against Automated Brute-Force Attacks
description: Administrative access interfaces must incorporate defenses against automated dictionary and brute-force attacks.
rationale: Rate-limits automated authentication attempts.

title: Network Security - Ingress Filtering and Source Routing Elimination
description: IP packets specifying explicit source routing paths must be dropped by network routing infrastructure.
rationale: Ensures traffic strictly follows designated security monitoring boundaries.

title: Network Security - Elimination of ICMP Route Injections and Redirects
description: Routers shall not broadcast ICMP redirect directives that could alter adjacent host route metrics.
rationale: Prevents route manipulation on local network segments.

title: Network Security - Prevention of Amplified Directed Broadcasts
description: Subnet directed broadcast forwarding shall be disabled to avoid participating in denial-of-service amplification.
rationale: Mitigates reflection and amplification attack vectors.

title: Network Security - Mitigation of ARP Poisoning and Insecure Proxy ARP
description: Proxy ARP functionality must be disabled on all active routed interfaces.
rationale: Protects against address resolution spoofing and topology reconnaissance.

title: Network Security - Ingress IP Anti-Spoofing via Unicast RPF
description: Network edge interfaces shall enforce source address verification via Unicast Reverse Path Forwarding.
rationale: Drops illegitimate packets with fabricated sender IPs.

title: Logging - Millisecond Timestamp Precision for Event Correlation
description: Event logging records shall include high-resolution timestamps with timezone definitions for audit accuracy.
rationale: Critical for cross-system log correlation during incident forensics.

title: Logging - Resilient Local Logging Buffer Configuration
description: Sufficient internal buffer space must be configured to retain operational security logs locally.
rationale: Ensures log availability even when outbound network connectivity is interrupted.

title: Logging - Cryptographically Authenticated Clock Synchronization
description: Time synchronization protocols shall be cryptographically authenticated to preserve clock integrity.
rationale: Prevents unauthorized time skew attacks.

title: Use of Cryptography - Robust Cryptographic Protection for SNMPv3
description: Network management telemetry and control channels shall enforce AES cryptographic encryption (authPriv).
rationale: Protects management messages against unauthorized eavesdropping.

title: Network Security - Control Plane Protection and Traffic Throttling
description: Protective mechanisms such as Control Plane Policing shall be deployed to prevent control plane overload.
rationale: Ensures uninterrupted operation of core routing engines during attacks.

title: Network Security - Cryptographic Routing Peer Verification
description: Dynamic routing protocols must authenticate peer routers cryptographically to ensure topology integrity.
rationale: Prevents unauthorized route injection.

title: Logging - Centralized Command and Administrative Event Accounting
description: Administrative actions and privileged commands shall be recorded in centralized accounting logs.
rationale: Guarantees full accountability for administrative activities.

title: Network Security - Restriction of Layer 2 Discovery Protocols on Untrusted Links
description: Unsolicited layer-2 neighbor discovery advertisements (CDP/LLDP) shall be restricted on untrusted links.
rationale: Minimizes automated topology reconnaissance by unauthorized actors.
